en.title: Facebook, Instagram, Gmail or Social Media Account Hacked: What to Do
en.directAnswer: Use the platform's official account-recovery process first. Change the password if you still have access. Remove unknown devices and recovery details. Turn on two-factor authentication. Save emails showing password, email or phone changes. Warn your contacts if the attacker is sending messages from your account. If the attacker stole information, demanded money, committed fraud or continues to access the account, preserve the evidence and consider a formal report.

steps: Submit the application or complaint to the designated authority.
Retain all receipts and acknowledgment slips.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: A person's Facebook password stops working. Friends then receive messages asking for emergency money. The user should start Facebook's official hacked-account recovery, secure the email account connected to Facebook, warn contacts, preserve the scam messages, and report any financial fraud separately.
en.specialistTrigger: Business account takeover; stolen client data; financial loss; repeated harassment; blackmail; intimate-image misuse; or a dispute involving contractual or commercial damage.
